text:
Maya (CEO): Thanks for coming to the all-hands. Opening a short follow-up thread focused on the strategy Qs we didn't get to. Keep replies brief and action-oriented.

Marco (Sales): Need a crisp way to explain why customers choose Redwood vs "build-your-own" — what's the simplest elevator line?

Maya (CEO): Try: 'We turn models into reliable features — less ops, predictable performance, and enterprise controls.' That's the hook; Sales, trim for decks.

Roxanne (Marketing): For external comms, can we lead with a benefit instead of tech terms? Something like 'Make model features dependable' vs 'inference platform'.

Priya (Head of Product): Agreed. Benefit-led hero works better for PLG. We'll keep a developer-facing page with deeper infra language.

Ellen (Field Engineer): Field note: prospects often ask about how we avoid cost spikes when traffic is bursty. What's the approved line?

Jon (CTO): Say: we smooth bursts with adaptive batching, prefix caching, and policy-driven routing — so peak cost is controlled and SLOs are preserved. If asked for numbers, point them to the published conservative benchmarks.

Marco (Sales): Sales triggers — can we formalize what moves a trial into a sales conversation? Right now it's fuzzy.

Priya (Head of Product): New rule proposal: move to sales when any of these are met: sustained usage > $6k/mo, explicit ask for Private or KMS, p95 latency breaches 3 times in a week, or regulatory/compliance mention. I'll add to the playbook this week.

Roxanne (Marketing): Can Legal pre-clear two short performance lines we can use publicly? Need low-risk numbers for website and decks.

Maya (CEO): Legal and Finance will bless conservative metrics. Proposed safe lines: 'median request latency ~100ms for common decoder models' and 'typical TCO improvements 30% vs unmanaged fleets'. Tag as illustrative until signed.

Ellen (Field Engineer): For demo scripts, can we get a simple policy YAML showing graceful degradation? Sales wants pasteable snippets.

Jon (CTO): Use this minimal example for slides:
```
route_policy:
  primary: latency
  secondary: cost
  fallback: quantized_small
  canary: 5%
```
It communicates routing priorities and fallback without heavy infra detail.

Marco (Sales): For competitor questions: some vendors emphasize 'fastest model access' and 'daily weight updates'. How should we answer?

Maya (CEO): Acknowledge freshness matters, then pivot: freshness is only valuable if the model runs reliably in production. Our differentiation is operational discipline: rollouts with SLO gates, transparent metrics, and cost controls.

Priya (Head of Product): Small product ask: we'll publish a "what winning looks like" page in Confluence — short list of metrics for teams (latency, cost per 1k tokens, error rate). I will draft and request Jon for numbers.

OpsBot: Recording and slides uploaded: https://redwood.internal/all-hands/2322223333/recording

Roxanne (Marketing): Who owns the enterprise one-liner that calls out Private + KMS + SLA? Need sign-off for decks ASAP.

Maya (CEO): Priya draft, Jon confirm technical accuracy, Legal + Sales will sign off. Suggested starter: 'Private deployments, KMS integrations, and SLA-backed uptime.'

Ellen (Field Engineer): Last practical Q — any change to the default demo environment so Sales can reproduce latency examples?

Jon (CTO): We'll create a Sales demo slice with controlled workloads and a readout of median/p95 latencies. Ops, please allocate a small canary pool for that.

Priya (Head of Product): I'll collect action items and post the playbook link in this channel when ready.

Maya (CEO): Thanks all. If no more Qs, I’ll close this thread at EOD and circulate the action list. :sparkles:
